verifier_owned_fixture.scenario: Call G1->G2 ACK completion twice with identical mission/step/state fingerprint/transfer_id/handoff sequence while omitting consumed_transfer_ids, which the public overlap_shift API currently permits.
verifier_owned_fixture.observed: Both acknowledged calls return SHIFT_COMPLETE with execution_authorized=true because consumed_transfer_ids=None creates a fresh ephemeral set on every call.
verifier_owned_fixture.expected: Exactly-once torque transfer must be machine-enforced. The API must require authoritative idempotency state or otherwise persist/derive a durable consume token; omission must fail closed rather than silently degrade to replayable execution.

root_cause: `overlap_shift(..., consumed_transfer_ids=None)` silently substitutes a new local set(), so completed-transfer consumption is lost between calls.
Exactly-once safety therefore depends on every caller remembering to pass durable idempotency state; the function itself permits a replayable unsafe mode.
`receiver_transfer_id` is also optional, so the repaired path remains permissive rather than fail-closed at the transfer boundary.
repair_acceptance: Make authoritative consumed-transfer/idempotency state mandatory for any ACK-capable shift completion; if missing, fail closed with GearboxGuardError or equivalent non-executing result.
Require receiver_transfer_id for completion after receiver ACK; missing identity must not authorize SHIFT_COMPLETE/DOWNSHIFT_COMPLETE.
Keep deterministic transfer_id binding to mission_id, step_id, from_gear, to_gear, state_fingerprint and handoff_sequence.
Add verifier-visible tests for missing consumed state, missing receiver transfer identity, duplicate ACK replay, stale ACK and wrong transfer identity.
Preserve RPM continuity, compact no-raw-chat handoff, lower-guard-first downshift, exact A/B/C topology, storage/progress/metabolism guards.
